title: King Oliver and Williams's blues-contest recordings
summary: Oliver sometimes recorded with Williams; Williams hired trumpeters for blues contest winners and chose men by results; Allen names the bands he worked with.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Well he was about anything class way man, King Oliver had something in there to do, he'd come to record it. Whenever he come in time, he'd make some recordings with his band. And most of the time King Oliver made his own band so he didn't have to have nobody. When Clarence was going to make something from his group, he'd set King in and all that. Always make some money see. Well Williams didn't have a regular group working anyway. No, I don't remember having a group in any spot at all. But most of the time he relied on his recording. Of course he didn't play that with everybody, record for everybody. Blues, singers and all. I'd like to tell you the other part of the first I taught them, there were contests all over the country, and they'd make the blues come and send a particular okay record. They'd come to New York's little wonder blues contest, but send them to New York to do the recording. And they'd call Glass and say, I got recorded, you know, I want to need a trumpet player, I need a piano player, you want to come out and play for this? He'd say, no, quite never, I got to turn it recording. I'd go out and make one record out of the room there. He said, I got recorded in the morning on a trumpet player, you want to go out and make it? I said, well yeah. I've made records I never heard of before, I'd never seen them. I'm going to go again about it. How they sound, good or bad, they'll pick a different out of the money. Well he certainly got good men. He always tried to get good men. Otherwise they would come back, if he got a recording, he didn't think it was good. He was that smart, he'd get somebody else. Next time, he'd call and so on and so on. He got them out of all the different bands. Different bands, different musicians in town. And he practically knew everybody. He even got them running by. Clarence got recorded, he was calling him Cuzz. Cuzz, what you got up? Can you go on some of your recording dates that they come up? You know something? He said, yeah, come on now, Cuzz. Come on, I got a date, so, so, so. He's going to give you a ring. He said, well, he said, we telegram. I wasn't living with him. He said, we telegram. I got recorded, text the date. Be down in the office or be down in the studio. So he text the date and we were all naked.

That's a good record. With whose band were you working at the time you made most of your recordings for Clarence Williams? Once I was working with Alain Rolf and Leroy Tiff, the band saved by Connie Zinn.
That was a Connie Zinn band. Yeah. Alain Rolf had a band first when he left, and Leroy Tiff took over. That was about three or two or three years later.
